# LeakSanitizer suppressions for ci.yml's asan job (LSAN_OPTIONS=suppressions=...).
#
# An entry must name an internal function of a third-party
# component that makes a one-time allocation (process-lifetime cache, static
# initialization) or a per-thread allocation it never frees by design, with a
# comment saying why. Never name a library
# (leak:libGLESv2) or an exported EGL/GL/Vulkan entry point (leak:eglInitialize):
# either hides every unreachable allocation made under it, including ones our
# own misuse causes. The published ANGLE libraries are stripped, so the asan
# job builds with OXGL_ANGLE_SYMBOLS=1: the tests then load the unstripped
# libraries from the platform's pinned symbols archive (angle/bundles.toml),
# and entries can name ANGLE-internal functions.

# ANGLE allocates each thread's egl::Thread (and its Display TLS) on the
# thread's first EGL call and intentionally never frees it: 72 bytes per thread
# that used EGL (README, Known issues). Test threads exit before LeakSanitizer
# runs. Seen on Linux arm64 only. Rechecked on each ANGLE update (angle/README.md,
# "Known upstream issues").
leak:egl::GetCurrentThread
